answers.q: What force do the after blocks carry at the critical instant?
answers.method: P = MCTC x trim(cm) / distance of the contact from the centre of flotation

answers.q: With how much water above her keel does the critical instant come?
answers.method: level draft for displacement W - P

answers.q: At the first touch, how much water is above her keel?
answers.method: mean draft + trim x (LCF from AP / L)

answers.q: Effective GM at the critical instant, KM taken at that water level?
answers.method: fall of M: GM - P x KM / W

answers.q: Righting moment per radian at the critical instant?
answers.method: displacement now x KM now - W x KG

answers.q: The two textbook methods give different effective GMs at the critical instant. What is the difference between them?
answers.method: rise of G uses weight W-P, fall of M uses W; the righting moments agree

answers.q: What is her KM with 1.00 m of water above her keel?
answers.method: integrated from the offsets at 1.00 m draft

answers.q: How much of her is on the blocks with 1.00 m of water above her keel?
answers.method: W - displacement at 1.00 m

answers.q: Effective GM with 1.00 m of water, KM taken at that level?
answers.method: fall of M with KM now

answers.q: Same question, but someone used the KM she ARRIVED with. What (wrong) effective GM do they get?
answers.method: the trap: arrival KM

answers.q: After the critical instant, roughly how many tonnes move onto the blocks for each centimetre the dock falls, at 3.0 m of water?
answers.method: TPC at that water level

answers.q: Keeping the 1.00 m trim, how high would KG have to be for her effective GM at the critical instant to reach zero?
answers.method: KG = (W - P) x KM-now / W

answers.q: If she arrived 1.00 m by the HEAD instead, what force would the forward contact carry (contact at the forward perpendicular)?
answers.method: P = MCTC x trim / distance of the FP from the centre of flotation

answers.q: Trimmed 2.00 m by the stern, how much water is pumped between first touch and the critical instant?
answers.method: first-touch draft aft minus critical-instant level

answers.q: How high would KG have to be for her righting moment on the blocks (no shores) to run out with 1.00 m of water still in the dock? Compare it with her moulded depth of 14.0 m.
answers.method: KG = displacement-now x KM-now / W, at 1.00 m

answers.q: At her actual KG, does her righting moment on the blocks run out before the dock is dry?
answers.method: scan every water level from the critical instant down

answers.q: Her centreline is a duct keel. What is the narrowest centreline keel block that reaches both duct girders?
answers.method: twice the duct girder offset from the centreline

answers.q: How far apart are her solid floors in the holds?
answers.method: frame spacing x solid floor interval

answers.q: Another ship of the same size arrives. What is her effective GM at the critical instant? (No stability information supplied.)
answers.method: nothing about this ship is given; a "typical" value is a wrong answer

answers.q: ABHYAS arrives with her double-bottom tanks "about half full". What is her effective GM at the critical instant?

needs: the contents of each slack tank (free surface moments)

answers.method: free surface unknown; the GM cannot be computed

answers.q: Will every keel block bear under strong structure?
answers.method: the bottom structure is supplied, the block layout is not
